candidates.name: Discoid lupus erythematosus
support_spans: The patient denied any trauma history and had no history of connective tissue disease nor any evidence of systemic involvement, such as arthralgia, photosensitivity, or skin rashes.
contradict_spans: The result of a hair pull test was negative.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves and localized linear hair loss is consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

candidates.name: Lichen planopilaris
support_spans: Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation; however, broken hairs were not seen.
candidates.why: The dermoscopic findings and the presence of lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis are consistent with lichen planopilaris.

candidates.name: Frontal fibrosing alopecia
support_spans: The patient reported that when the lesion had begun approximately 10 years earlier, he had received 2 doses of intralesional steroid via injection on a small bald patch on the vertex.
candidates.why: The patient's history of gradual progression of the lesion and the presence of linear hair loss are consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia.

candidates.name: Alopecia areata
support_spans: The result of a hair pull test was negative.
contradict_spans: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves and localized linear hair loss is not typical of alopecia areata.
candidates.why: The negative hair pull test and the presence of short vellus hairs are consistent with alopecia areata, but the patient's presentation is not typical.

candidates.name: Morphaea
support_spans: The lesions measured (length × width) 7 × 2 cm and 6 × 1 cm, respectively.
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of linear, depressed skin grooves is consistent with morphea.

candidates.name: Lupus erythematosus
support_spans: Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
candidates.why: The positive direct immunofluorescence and the presence of granular deposition of immunoglobulins and complement components are consistent with lupus erythematosus.

candidates.name: Autoimmune alopecia
support_spans: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves and localized linear hair loss is consistent with autoimmune alopecia.

candidates.name: Inflammatory alopecia

candidates.why: The presence of lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis are consistent with inflammatory alopecia.
